short: The broad field of building computer systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence.
eli5: Teaching a computer to notice patterns, solve puzzles, and make helpful choices on its own.
example: A navigation app predicting traffic jams and suggesting a faster route.

short: A branch of AI where algorithms improve their performance on a task by learning patterns from data rather than following hardcoded rules.
eli5: Instead of writing a strict recipe, you show the computer thousands of finished dishes until it figures out how to cook.
example: A spam filter learning which words signal junk mail from millions of labeled emails.

short: Training a model on input-output pairs where every training example comes with a known correct answer.
eli5: Studying with flashcards that have the question on the front and the answer on the back.
example: Training a house-price predictor using past sales records with square footage and actual sale prices.

short: Discovering hidden structure, groups, or patterns in data without any human-provided labels.
eli5: Sorting a mixed pile of LEGO bricks into groups by shape and color without anyone telling you the group names.
example: Grouping online shoppers into distinct purchasing personas based solely on browsing behavior.

short: A supervised learning task that assigns an input to one of several predefined discrete categories.
eli5: Sorting incoming mail into labeled bins like 'Bills', 'Friends', or 'Spam'.
example: Predicting whether a medical scan shows a benign or malignant tumor.

short: A supervised learning task that predicts a continuous numerical quantity rather than a category.
eli5: Guessing how many inches tall a puppy will grow based on its paws and parents.
example: Forecasting tomorrow's electricity demand in megawatts from weather and calendar data.

short: A flowchart-like model that makes predictions by splitting data through a sequence of simple if-then feature questions.
eli5: Playing a game of Twenty Questions where each yes-or-no answer narrows down the final guess.
example: A loan screening tree checking income above $50k, then credit history, then debt ratio.

short: An ensemble algorithm that trains many diverse decision trees on random data subsets and combines their votes.
eli5: Asking a hundred different experts for their opinion and going with the majority vote so one person's mistake doesn't ruin the answer.
example: Predicting customer churn reliably across tabular CRM metrics without heavy tuning.

short: A classical classifier that finds the separating boundary with the widest possible safety margin between classes.
eli5: Drawing the widest possible road down the middle between two neighborhoods so neither side's houses are close to the line.
example: Separating handwritten digit classes in compact feature spaces using a kernel boundary.

short: An unsupervised algorithm that partitions data points into k groups by iteratively assigning points to the nearest cluster center.
eli5: Dropping k flags on a playground, having kids stand by the closest flag, then moving each flag to the center of its group.
example: Compressing an image's color palette down to its 16 most representative colors.

short: When a model memorizes noise and quirks in the training data so closely that it performs poorly on new, unseen examples.
eli5: Memorizing the exact practice test questions instead of learning the math, then failing when the real test changes the numbers.
example: A curve that zigzags through every training point at 100% accuracy but misses new test points wildly.

short: The fundamental balance between underfitting from overly simple assumptions (bias) and overfitting to training noise (variance).
eli5: A bow that always shoots too far left has high bias; a bow that scatters arrows everywhere has high variance.
example: Choosing tree depth in a model so it captures real trends without memorizing random fluctuations.
